graham.brief:
Jaylen Warren has a 15.5 rush attempts line this week, a long way from his season. Through three games, Warren is averaging 12.7 rush attempts. The books look for about 21 points from Pittsburgh, with a 38.5 total on the game. What would have to change for Pittsburgh to lean on Warren more?

Begin with how much Pittsburgh leaned on Warren last week. Warren's volume climbed from 15 to 21 last week. That kind of jump can mean Pittsburgh has handed Warren a bigger job.

Warren is the whole question. Perhaps his recent workload matters most here, or perhaps three games of Warren just make a noisy baseline. Warren hasn't played enough yet for his average to count as a tendency.

Watch whether Pittsburgh keeps handing to Warren after the first series, because that answers it faster than his average.
